info.title: MonoCloud Management API
info.description: The MonoCloud Management API provides endpoints for configuring and managing identity infrastructure, including clients, protected resources, users, groups, security controls, cryptographic keys, mTLS configuration, and platform settings within the MonoCloud platform.

get.description: Retrieves a paginated list of applications. Optional query parameters allow searching, filtering, and sorting the results.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page number to retrieve.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: The number of client applications to return per page.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Optional Lucene-style filter expression used to search by attributes.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort expression in the format `field:direction`, where direction is `1` for ascending or `-1` for descending. Supported fields include - `client_name` and `creation_time`

200.description: The applications were retrieved successfully

Indicates whether the consents are enabled for the client.
>[!note]
> Secure+ subscription required to use consents.

require_consent.description:
Controls whether users are prompted to review and approve requested permissions.
>[!note]
> Secure+ subscription required to use consents.

always_require_consent_for_offline_acces.description:
Always prompts users for consent when requesting offline (refresh token) access.
>[!note]
> This setting applies even if the user previously chose to remember their consent.
Secure+ subscription required to use consents.

remember_consent.description: Controls how consent decisions are remembered for future sign-ins.

show_consent_scope_selection.description:
Allows end users to choose which requested scopes to grant on the consent screen.
>[!note]
> Secure+ subscription required to use consents.

always_include_user_claims_in_id_token.description:
Always embeds user claims in the ID token instead of requiring calls to the `UserInfo` endpoint.
>[!note]
> Enabling this increases the ID token size and may expose more user data to applications than necessary.

allowed_grant_types.description:
Defines which OAuth / OIDC grant types this client is permitted to use.
>[!note]
> Only valid and secure grant combinations are supported.

require_pkce.description:
Requires Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) for authorization code flows.
>[!note]
> Strongly recommended for public clients such as SPAs and mobile applications.

allow_plain_text_pkce.description:
Allows Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) verification using the plain (unhashed) method.
>[!warning]
> Use only for legacy compatibility — strongly discouraged for production.

require_request_object.description:
Requires authorization requests to be sent as signed JWT request objects (JAR).
>[!note]
> Secure+ subscription required to use JWT request objects (JAR).

require_pushed_authorization_requests.description:
Requires clients to use Pushed Authorization Requests (PAR) instead of sending parameters directly to the authorization endpoint.
>[!note]
> Secure+ subscription required to use Pushed Authorization Requests (PAR).

allow_any_pushed_authorization_redirect_.description:
Allows the client to use any redirect URI when using Pushed Authorization Requests (PAR), instead of being limited to the configured redirect URI list.
>[!note]
> Secure+ subscription required to use Pushed Authorization Requests (PAR).

authorization_request_lifetime.description: Lifetime of the authorization request (in seconds). Controls how long the request data is considered valid during the authorization flow.

allow_access_tokens_via_browser.description:
Controls whether access tokens may be transmitted via the browser for this client.
>[!warning]
> Enable only when absolutely necessary. Returning access tokens to the browser increases the risk of leakage through logs, plugins, redirects, or malicious scripts. Recommended to keep disabled and prefer the Authorization Code + PKCE flow.

redirect_uris.description:
List of approved redirect URIs where authorization codes or tokens may be sent.
>[!note]
> Only exact, fully-qualified matches are allowed.

post_logout_redirect_uris.description:
List of approved URIs users can be redirected to after a successful logout.
>[!note]
> Only exact, fully-qualified matches are allowed.

front_channel_logout_uri.description:
Browser-based (front-channel) endpoint on the client that receives user logout notifications from MonoCloud.
>[!note]
> Pro plan subscription required to use front-channel logout.

front_channel_logout_session_required.description:
Indicates whether the user’s session identifier should be included when invoking the front-channel logout URI.
>[!note]
> Pro plan subscription required to use front-channel logout.

back_channel_logout_uri.description:
Server-side (back-channel) endpoint that MonoCloud calls to notify the application of a user logout.
>[!note]
> Secure+ subscription required to use back-channel logout.

back_channel_logout_session_required.description:
Indicates whether the user’s session identifier should be included when invoking the back-channel logout URI.
>[!note]
> Secure+ subscription required to use back-channel logout.

bind_refresh_tokens_to_session.description:
Binds refresh tokens issued for the client to the user's session. When enabled, refresh tokens are automatically revoked when the user signs out or the session expires.
>[!note]
> ScaleX subscription required to use session binding.

allow_offline_access.description:
Allows the client to obtain refresh tokens using the `offline_access` scope.
>[!note]
> Use only for trusted applications that can securely store long-lived tokens.

allowed_identity_scopes.description: Defines the approved identity scopes that this client is authorized to request.

identity_token_lifetime.description: Specifies how long an ID token remains valid (in seconds).

access_token_lifetime.description: Specifies how long access tokens issued without API resource scopes remain valid (in seconds). These tokens may only be used with the UserInfo endpoint.

authorization_code_lifetime.description: Specifies how long an authorization code remains valid (in seconds).

consent_lifetime.description:
Specifies the validity period for stored user consent (in seconds). Set to `0` to allow consent to remain valid indefinitely.
>[!note]
> Secure+ subscription required to use consents.

absolute_refresh_token_lifetime.description:
Specifies the maximum lifetime of a refresh token (in seconds), regardless of how often it is used.
>[!note]
> ScaleX subscription required to configure refresh token lifetimes longer than a month.

sliding_refresh_token_lifetime.description: Defines the sliding expiration window for refresh tokens (in seconds). Token expiry is extended on each valid refresh, subject to the absolute refresh token lifetime.

refresh_token_usage.description: Controls whether refresh tokens are single-use (rotated) or reusable.

update_access_token_claims_on_refresh.description: Controls whether access token claims are recalculated and reissued when refreshing a token.

emit_offline_access_scope_in_access_toke.description: Includes the `offline_access` scope in issued access tokens when requested by the client.

refresh_token_expiration.description: Controls whether refresh tokens expire at a fixed time or are extended with continued use.

access_token_type.description: Specifies whether access tokens issued without API resource scopes are issued as self-contained JWTs or opaque reference tokens. These tokens may only be used with the UserInfo endpoint.

authenticator_restrictions.description:

>[!note]
> ScaleX subscription required to use session binding.

allow_offline_access.description:
Allows the client to obtain refresh tokens using the `offline_access` scope.
>[!note]
> Use only for trusted applications that can securely store long-lived tokens.

authorization_code_lifetime.description: Specifies how long an authorization code remains valid (in seconds).

consent_lifetime.description:
Specifies the validity period for stored user consent (in seconds). Set to `0` to allow consent to remain valid indefinitely.
>[!note]
> Secure+ subscription required to use consents.

absolute_refresh_token_lifetime.description:
Specifies the maximum lifetime of a refresh token (in seconds), regardless of how often it is used.
>[!note]
> ScaleX subscription required to configure refresh token lifetimes longer than a month.

sliding_refresh_token_lifetime.description: Defines the sliding expiration window for refresh tokens (in seconds). Token expiry is extended on each valid refresh, subject to the absolute refresh token lifetime.

refresh_token_usage.description: Controls whether refresh tokens are single-use (rotated) or reusable.

update_access_token_claims_on_refresh.description: Controls whether access token claims are recalculated and reissued when refreshing a token.
